localBiteReport: Reports from the past week to two weeks on Choctawhatchee Bay point to a solid fall inshore bite. The most recent FishingBooker angler report (posted approximately 7 days ago) describes a successful charter trip that included two keeper-sized redfish caught near a bridge, consistent with the fall pattern when reds stage around structure. A guide report from CaptainExperiences (posted roughly 1–2 weeks ago out of the Freeport/Destin area) notes that fishing has been productive overall, though quality fish have been a bit harder to come by, with live bait working best in the early morning and soft plastics carrying the bite through the rest of the day. Water temperature at this location is 70°F. Historically for mid-November on Choctawhatchee Bay, sheepshead and black drum begin showing up in force around bridge pilings and jetties as water cools, while speckled trout stack up in deeper bayous and creek mouths on the north and east ends of the bay — patterns consistent with what local guides and tackle shop reports have described for this time of year in recent seasons.
